best_architecture:
Recommended pattern is a three-tier memory hierarchy modeled on MemGPT's virtual-context/OS-paging analogy, mapped directly onto Local-Claw's existing stores, fronted by a hybrid-RAG retrieval pipeline and a strict token budgeter. (1) WORKING tier = the live Gemma context window, backed by Redis as a fast working-memory cache. It holds the system prompt, durable 'core memory' blocks (persona/user/task facts the agent can self-edit), a verbatim sliding window of the most recent turns, and the retrieved/compressed context for the current step. (2) SEMANTIC/ARCHIVAL tier = Chroma vector store for embeddings of facts, summaries, and documents, queried by RAG. (3) EPISODIC tier = MongoDB full session history (every raw message), the durable cold store / 'recall storage' that can be searched and re-summarized. The agent moves data between tiers via explicit tool calls (e.g. archival_memory_search, core_memory_append/replace, conversation_search) exactly as in the MemGPT/Letta design, so the LLM itself decides what to page in.

Retrieval into the working tier should be a HYBRID RAG pipeline, not vector-only, because vector search misses literal tokens (error codes, flags, file paths, IDs) that matter for a coding/agent harness: run BM25 (lexical, e.g. rank_bm25 or Chroma's full-text) and dense vector search (Chroma) in parallel, fuse the two ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60, optionally weighted e.g. dense 0.7 / lexical 0.3 since RRF needs no score normalization), then re-rank the fused top ~50 candidates with a cross-encoder reranker (e.g. BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 or cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) down to the top 5-10 that actually enter the window.

CONTEXT COMPRESSION is essential to keep the working tier within budget: keep recent turns verbatim, and once older history exceeds a threshold, summarize it (LangChain's ConversationSummaryBufferMemory pattern: token-length-triggered, not turn-count-triggered). Use Chain-of-Density (Adams et al. 2023) prompting to produce dense, entity-rich summaries of episodic history at fixed length before they are stored back as semantic memory or kept as a rolling summary buffer.

The most important design decisions: (a) TOKEN BUDGETING is the central control loop -- allocate the fixed Gemma window into explicit sub-budgets (system+core memory, sliding window, retrieved RAG context, summary buffer, and a reserved completion margin), measure each component with the real tokenizer, and evict/compress lowest-priority content first when over budget. Never let the sum exceed the window minus generation reserve, or you OOM/truncate. (b) Avoid 'memory blindness' -- aggressive archiving means the agent forgets that a fact even exists in cold storage; keep lightweight pointers/keywords in the working tier and make retrieval reliable. (c) Hybrid retrieval + reranking, not naive top-k vector, is what makes the semantic tier trustworthy for an agent. (d) Self-editing core memory blocks give durable, cheap context that survives every turn without re-retrieval. (e) Tier orchestration (what to page in/out and when) is the hardest part and the main source of quality loss, so make it explicit, observable, and tunable rather than purely LLM-self-diagnosed.
reference_papers: From Sparse to Dense: GPT-4 Summarization with Chain of Density Prompting (Adams et al. 2023) - arxiv:2309.04269 (also ACL 4th New Frontiers in Summarization Workshop) - the Chain-of-Density iterative summarization method for compressing history into dense, entity-rich, fixed-length summaries

MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems (Packer et al. 2023) - arxiv:2310.08560 - virtual context management with OS-style memory paging across main context / recall storage / archival storage tiers; the foundational tiered-memory design

Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey (Gao et al. 2023/2024) - arxiv:2312.10997 - canonical RAG survey covering naive/advanced/modular RAG, retrieval, reranking and fusion

Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual Rank Learning Methods (Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher 2009) - SIGIR 2009 - origin of the RRF algorithm used to fuse BM25 and dense rankings [uncertain: exact venue/year recall]
Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering (Karpukhin et al. 2020) - arxiv:2004.04906 - dense bi-encoder retrieval, the vector half of hybrid RAG

LoCoMo: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents (Maharana et al. 2024) - arxiv:2402.17753 - benchmark for very long-term memory (up to 35 sessions / 300+ turns); shows RAG-augmented LLMs still lag humans [uncertain: exact arxiv id]
Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents / CoALA (Sumers et al. 2024) - arxiv:2309.02427 - working/episodic/semantic/procedural memory taxonomy for LLM agents
A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents (Xu et al. 2025) - arxiv:2502.12110 - dynamic, self-organizing agent memory

Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers (2026) - arxiv:2603.07670 - recent survey of tiered/hierarchical agent memory, retrieval, and evaluation [uncertain: arxiv id/date may be a preprint placeholder]
reference_repos: letta-ai/letta - platform for stateful agents with self-editing tiered memory (the production successor to MemGPT; implements core/recall/archival memory and memory-management tools) - https://github.com/letta-ai/letta

mem0ai/mem0 - universal memory layer for AI agents; multi-signal retrieval (semantic + BM25 keyword + entity matching fused), temporal reasoning; strong LoCoMo/LongMemEval scores - https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0
langchain-ai/langchain - ConversationSummaryBufferMemory and related memory utilities (token-triggered summary buffering) - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain

run-llama/llama_index - QueryFusionRetriever (BM25 + vector with reciprocal-rerank fusion) and node-postprocessor rerankers (SentenceTransformerRerank, CohereRerank) - https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index
UKPLab/sentence-transformers - bi-encoder embeddings and CrossEncoder rerankers for the retrieve-and-rerank pipeline - https://github.com/UKPLab/sentence-transformers
FlagOpen/FlagEmbedding - BGE embeddings and BGE rerankers (FlagReranker, bge-reranker-v2-m3), top open-weight reranker - https://github.com/FlagOpen/FlagEmbedding
dorianbrown/rank_bm25 - lightweight pure-Python BM25 implementation for the lexical half of hybrid retrieval - https://github.com/dorianbrown/rank_bm25
chroma-core/chroma - the vector DB used by Local-Claw for the semantic tier (supports embeddings + full-text/keyword) - https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma
tim-ponomarev/hybrid-rag - production-grade reference pipeline: BM25 + dense retrieval + RRF + cross-encoder reranking + LLM-as-Judge - https://github.com/tim-ponomarev/hybrid-rag

NirDiamant/Agent_Memory_Techniques - 30 runnable notebooks covering buffers, vector stores, episodic/semantic memory, MemGPT, Mem0, Letta, Zep, LoCoMo - https://github.com/NirDiamant/Agent_Memory_Techniques
key_libraries: chromadb (Python) - vector store for the semantic/archival tier; supports dense vector + metadata + full-text search. Use latest 0.5.x+
redis / redis-py (Python) - working-memory cache for the live tier (recent turns, session scratch, retrieval cache)
pymongo / motor (Python) - access to MongoDB episodic store (full raw session history); motor for async
rank_bm25 (Python, v0.2.2) - BM25Okapi lexical retrieval for hybrid RAG when not using Chroma's built-in full-text
sentence-transformers (Python, v3.x+) - bi-encoder embedding models and CrossEncoder reranker (e.g. cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2)
FlagEmbedding (Python) - BGE embeddings + FlagReranker for BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 (best open-weight reranker, runs on CPU for small batches)
langchain / langchain-community (Python) - ConversationSummaryBufferMemory and EnsembleRetriever (weighted BM25+vector fusion) for memory + token-triggered summarization
llama-index / llama-index-core (Python) - QueryFusionRetriever (RRF fusion of BM25+vector) and SentenceTransformerRerank node postprocessor

tiktoken or the Gemma/HF tokenizer (transformers AutoTokenizer) - exact token counting for the token-budget control loop (use the actual Gemma tokenizer, not tiktoken's GPT vocab, for accuracy) [uncertain: Gemma ships its own SentencePiece tokenizer via transformers; tiktoken is GPT-specific]
letta (Python) - optional full framework if adopting the MemGPT tiered-memory + self-editing-memory-tool pattern wholesale rather than building it
mem0ai (Python/Node) - optional drop-in memory layer with built-in hybrid (semantic+BM25+entity) retrieval and temporal reasoning
uncertain: Exact venue/year for the original Reciprocal Rank Fusion paper (cited as Cormack et al. SIGIR 2009)
Exact arxiv id for LoCoMo (given as 2402.17753) and for the 2026 'Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents' survey (2603.07670 appears to be a future/preprint-style id)

Whether to use tiktoken vs the native Gemma SentencePiece tokenizer for token budgeting -- Gemma is not a GPT/tiktoken model, so the HF AutoTokenizer for the specific Gemma checkpoint is the accurate choice
Optimal RRF weighting (e.g. dense 0.7 / lexical 0.3) and reranker candidate-pool size are domain-dependent and must be tuned on Local-Claw's own data
